code_findings.claim: An in-place Hermes patch transaction already exists from the earlier bridge-first design
That transaction stops and verifies only hermes-gateway.service; the dashboard, CLI sessions, cron workers, and other profiles keep running old code
Its post-restart check does not verify that the new process exposes the patched hooks or required middleware
Its journal and file writes use os.replace without fsync, unlike ProgramTransaction.publish
The bridge silently registers reduced stock hooks when patched hooks are absent
Lasting-memory ownership fails closed on a host without REQUIRED_MIDDLEWARE_API_VERSION
The managed release copies the complete patched Hermes tree, including .git, into each operation directory and repoints account launchers to it
Package and candidate validators require Git metadata (git rev-parse HEAD)
prepare_lifeos refuses whenever upstream LifeOS HEAD moves past the pinned commit
code_findings.kind: obsolete assumption for fetch on activation

code_findings.claim: Removal builds a second stock runtime from stock-hermes.tgz; it does not return to the user's original Hermes install
Removal refuses accounts with additional Hermes profiles
Every preparation downloads the full archive, dashboard, and Bun; no reuse or retention cleanup was found
code_findings.search: git grep rmtree|prune|retention|cleanup in the manager found only staging and grant cleanup

hermes_stock_facts.claim: Stock v0.21.7 base lacks pre_prompt_admission, pre_command_approval, augment_tool_result, pre_turn_stop, on_turn_result, pre_message_delivery
Stock register_hook and register_middleware accept unknown names with a warning
Stock middleware kinds are tool request, tool execution, LLM request, LLM execution; no required flag
Default Linux installer creates a Git checkout at HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent
Install provenance is an install stamp (docker, nix, desktop-app), live Git, or unknown
A tree with .git is treated as a dev checkout, never a sealed payload
hermes update autostashes local changes, then reapplies; on conflict it resets to clean and parks the stash
hermes update holds a kernel lock at <git common dir>/hermes-update.lock (or <install root>/.hermes-update.lock for ZIP installs)
When the configured memory provider is unavailable the agent runs without it and warns
Hermes-strict-inference keeps provider fallback by default (allow_provider_fallback=True)
hermes_stock_facts.scope: spot check of one patch only

hypotheses_untested: A user pm venv synced from the stock uv.lock plus Hermes plugin dependency install of the bridge reproduces the qualified 331-package closure
Holding the Hermes checkout update lock excludes a concurrent hermes update for the full patch transaction
The ten Hermes patches are behavior-neutral for profiles that do not load the bridge (only strict inference was spot-checked)
Fetching exactly one LifeOS or Hermes commit from GitHub is materially smaller than the full LifeOS clone or the stock archive
A .pth-installed import overlay can substitute patched modules before Hermes imports them and survives pm venv sync
Removing .git from the packaged runtime keeps Hermes identity, update refusal, and launcher behavior acceptable when an install stamp is written
On-disk use per retained operation is at least 1.08 GB (archive, extracted package, runtime copy, Bun archive); venv, Bun binary, reference .claude, and pm runtime are extra
Python wheel and LifeOS native package downloads per preparation (not measured; no network used)
